summary: Standing 54-ft Aermotor tower with 7x7 cab on Burke Mountain, Caledonia County, VT; NHLR-registered 1998; steps and cab rebuilt in 2023, railings added 2025.

facts.design: 54’ Aermotor tower with 7’ x 7’ steel cab
facts.agency: Vermont Dept. of Forests, Parks, and Recreation

access.note: Register says the tower, in Darling State Forest, is open to the public (line undated). A closure to the public from May 15 to July 31 (2025) was announced in a news article posted May 2, 2025, as part of a restoration project on state fire towers.

events.note: First lookout tower, built by Elmer A. Darling with a camp, per Forest Lookouts. The register dates the site's establishment to 1913.
Earliest staffing found: a lookoutman, Mr. Burrington, reported on Burke Mountain in the 8th Annual Report of the Vermont State Forester.
February 1932 newspaper: tower blown down. 1932 state report: tower collapsed under snow and ice. Sources disagree on the cause.
December 1934: an enclosed 45 ft. 6 in. steel tower erected on the identical site. A July 1935 newspaper also reports a new lookout tower on the summit.
Register: the wooden octagonal-cab tower was blown down in the great hurricane of 1937. Forest Lookouts lists 1937 but quotes a September 1938 newspaper saying a gale swept the tower from the peaks.
A 54-foot Aermotor tower with 7x7 cab completed, per Forest Lookouts. The register describes this as the current tower.
John Austin named as fire tower watchman and general caretaker of the Burke Mountain area.
John Dunphy began work at the forest fire tower in late April.
1957-58 state report: station converted from part time to full time, with a base radio installed in the tower and a remote control unit in the cabin.
Forest Lookouts: tower discontinued in the fall of 1984, one of the final two towers in use. The register instead says the tower was deactivated in the 1970s.
FAA gave the tower a facelift in exchange for hanging a microwave dish on it (register).
Registered September 1, 1998 as US 274, VT 5; nominated by Mark W. Haughwout, Vermont Registrar.
Register visit report dated September 2, 2006 answers the staffed question with No.
Vermont Forest, Parks and Recreation staff with a seasonal employee replaced all steps, landings and the cab floor with white oak on galvanized hardware.
Safety railing added to the cab floor; metal fencing installed along the sides, stairs and landings.
Tower maintenance completed at Okemo, Burke and Bear Hill: lightning protection, paint, interior cab railings, wire mesh on stairs and landings.
Closure to the public May 15 to July 31 announced in a news article posted May 2, 2025 (Bear Hill first, then Burke).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts dates the first tower and camp to 1912; the register says the site was established in 1913. Story reports both and does not pick one.
A February 1932 newspaper says wind blew the tower down; a 1932 state report says it collapsed under snow and ice. Not resolved.
The register says the 1937 hurricane took it; Forest Lookouts lists 1937 but quotes a September 1938 newspaper describing a gale. Not resolved.
Forest Lookouts says the tower was discontinued in fall 1984; the register says it was deactivated in the 1970s. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2007 'concrete steps repaired, no cab or tower work' event is not included. It appears only in a search snippet from cr-vt-2007.pdf (firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/cr-vt-2007.pdf), which was not read, so it is unverified here; worth a fetch and a quote. The 2025 MyChamplainValley closure notice is posted May 2, 2025, so the closure is now dated and used in the story. The register's 'open to the public' line is undated. Burke 54 ft matches brief height_m 16.5. Brief elevation_m 981.5 matches the register's 3,220 ft (981 m). Brief access 'unknown' is now public per the register. The Burlington Free Press 2025 article returned HTTP 403. Read budget used: 6 successful page reads plus one 403.
